title: Deuteronomy Bible Quiz - Chapter 17
description: Ten questions on Deuteronomy 17: witnesses, hard cases for the priests and judge, and the rules for a king.

questions.text: What kind of ox or sheep was not to be sacrificed to Yahweh?
questions.explanation: Verse 1 forbids sacrificing an ox or a sheep that has a defect or anything evil, because that is an abomination to Yahweh.

answers.text: One older than one year
A female animal
One bought from a foreigner
One with a defect or anything evil

questions.text: Besides other gods, what does verse 3 mention people wrongly worshiping?
questions.explanation: Verse 3 speaks of someone who served other gods and worshiped them, "or the sun, or the moon, or any of the stars of the sky."

answers.text: The great rivers and the depths of the seas
The sun, the moon or the stars
The clouds and the rain
The lightning and the thunder

questions.text: What does verse 6 say about witnesses when someone is to be put to death?
questions.explanation: He was to be put to death at the mouth of two or three witnesses; at the mouth of one witness he was not to be put to death.

answers.text: Two or three witnesses were needed, not one
One witness alone was always enough
Seven witnesses from the city were needed
Only the priest could act as a witness

questions.text: Whose hands were to be first on the guilty person to put him to death?
questions.explanation: Verse 7 says the hands of the witnesses were to be first on him, and afterward the hands of all the people.

answers.text: The hands of the priests
The hands of the elders
The hands of the witnesses
The hands of the judge

questions.text: Where were the people to go with a case that was too hard to judge?
questions.explanation: They were to go up to the place Yahweh chooses and come to the priests who are Levites and to the judge, who would give the verdict.

answers.text: To the king who sits in his palace
To the prophets of the land
To the elders of their own city
To the priests who are Levites and the judge

questions.text: What was to happen to the man who presumptuously refused to listen to the priest or the judge?
questions.explanation: Verse 12 says that man shall die, so the evil is put away from Israel.

answers.text: He was to die
He was to be sent out of the land
He was to pay a fine of silver
He was to be beaten with forty stripes

questions.text: According to verse 15, who must the king be?
questions.explanation: They were to set as king the one Yahweh chooses, one from among their brothers; they could not put a foreigner over them.

answers.text: A foreigner from a strong nation nearby
The oldest of the priests in the land
One from among their brothers, chosen by Yahweh
The man who owned the most horses

questions.text: For what purpose was the king not to cause the people to return to Egypt?
questions.explanation: The king was not to multiply horses, nor cause the people to return to Egypt in order to multiply horses.

answers.text: To buy grain
To hire soldiers
To trade in spices
To multiply horses

questions.text: Why was the king not to multiply wives to himself?
questions.explanation: Verse 17 says he shall not multiply wives to himself, "that his heart not turn away."

answers.text: So that he would not have too many sons to divide his kingdom
So that his heart would not turn away
So that the people would not be taxed
So that he could build a larger palace

questions.text: What was the king to write for himself when he sat on his throne?
questions.explanation: He was to write himself a copy of this law in a book and read from it all the days of his life.

answers.text: A record of all his battles and victories
A list of his officers
A copy of this law in a book
A song of victory
